title: F8Net: Fixed-Point 8-bit Only Multiplication for Network Quantization

summary: Snap Inc., Northeastern University and Rice University researchers position F8Net against the fixed-point quantization of Jain et al. (2019), which uses trainable power-of-two scale factors so that multiplication becomes bit shifting, and state that their work differs from it in three major aspects (pp. 2–3). They contrast F8Net's on-the-fly fractional length with TQT's directly trained fractional length (p. 7) and list TQT (Jain et al., 2019) in Table 1 for MobileNet V1 and V2b as the previous fixed-point quantization method (p. 8).

title: Improving Low-Precision Network Quantization via Bin Regularization
venue_basis: ICORE2026 A* venue; Uses or extends TQT
locator: Physical PDF p. 2 (printed p. 5242): related-work QAT citation group including [19]; p. 8 (printed p. 5248): Section 4.8 hardware-friendly baseline following [19, 21], Table 9 TQT, TQT+L2 and TQT+BR rows and the reported +3.7% over TQT; bibliography p. 9 (printed p. 5249), reference [19]
version: IEEE Xplore published print, ICCV 2021 proceedings
summary: Xilinx researchers in Beijing re-implement a hardware-friendly quantization baseline following references [19, 21], where [19] is TQT: power-of-two step sizes, low-bit first and last layers, quantized inputs and outputs of element-wise additions, 8-bit biases and batch normalization merged during training. They build bin regularization on this TQT baseline; Table 9 reports 63.8% top-1 for TQT, 65.8% for TQT+L2 and 67.5% for TQT+BR on 4-bit MobileNetV2, which the text describes as +3.7% over TQT (p. 8). Employer-linked: the authors list Xilinx Inc.
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: A Resource Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only FPGA-Based CNN Accelerator for Real-Time Facial Emotion Recognition
locator: Physical PDF pp. 3–4, 6–7, 10–12: TQT in related work, LLTQ proposed to address the disadvantages of previous works including TQT and derived as an alternative to TQT's power-of-two scale mapping, Figure 3, the implemented LSQ/TQT/LLTQ comparison and its Table 1 TQT row; bibliography p. 15, reference [39]
version: IEEE Access open-access publisher PDF
summary: Inha University and Sangmyung University researchers build log level threshold quantization (LLTQ) on TQT's power-of-two scale mapping, where a trainable log-threshold turns scale multiplication into shifts (p. 6). LLTQ maps the trainable parameter directly to a power-of-two scale and initializes activation scales from first-batch statistics in place of TQT's pre-calibration. They illustrate LSQ, TQT and LLTQ (Figure 3, p. 7), train all three (p. 10) and report TQT as hardware-friendly within about 0.45% of floating-point accuracy, a gap LLTQ closes (p. 11).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: Efficient SAR Vessel Detection for FPGA-Based On-Satellite Sensing
venue: SEC ’25, Tenth ACM/IEEE Symposium on Edge Computing (2025)
locator: Physical PDF p. 5, Section 3.2: INT8 Vitis AI quantization with power-of-two scaling and QAT using a straight-through estimator [35]; p. 11, Section 4.2.2, Table 4 and Section 4.3: QAT with a quantizer parameter learning rate and the deployed FPGA QAT models; bibliography p. 16, reference [35]
version: Published ACM version (open access, CC BY-NC 4.0)
summary: The Alan Turing Institute researchers deploy a YOLOv8-based SAR vessel detector on an AMD/Xilinx Kria KV260 FPGA, quantizing it to INT8 with the Vitis AI Quantizer using symmetric power-of-two scaling and quantization-aware training with a straight-through estimator, for which they cite TQT [35] (p. 5). They retrain with a tuned quantizer-parameter learning rate and report that the deployed QAT models match the expected GPU performance with little to no degradation (Table 4, Section 4.3, p. 11). TQT is cited by reference number rather than named, and is applied through the AMD/Xilinx Vitis AI toolchain.
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.
